stem: One bacterium divides, and the two daughter bacteria divide again. What causes the very minor differences among the four bacteria formed?
options: Mixing of DNA from two parents
Small inaccuracies in DNA copying
Fusion of male and female gametes
Changes caused by the surroundings
explanation: Correct option: (B). In asexual reproduction, the source of the minor differences described in the chapter is small inaccuracies in DNA copying. There is no mixing of DNA from two parents or fusion of gametes when a bacterium divides by itself, and the chapter does not attribute these differences to the surroundings.

stem: A field of sugarcane shows very little variation among plants, while a group of people shows quite distinct variations. Which explanation fits best?
options: Sugarcane is propagated vegetatively; humans reproduce sexually.
Sugarcane DNA is always copied without any errors at all.
People live in more varied surroundings than sugarcane does.
Sugarcane plants have far fewer genes than human beings.
explanation: Correct option: (A). Sugarcane is grown from stem cuttings, a form of asexual (vegetative) propagation, so variation arises only from small copying errors. Humans reproduce sexually, which combines DNA from two parents and generates much greater diversity. DNA copying is never perfectly accurate, and surroundings or gene number do not explain the difference.

stem: In an asexually reproducing species, trait A is found in 10% of the population and trait B in 60%. Which conclusion is most reasonable?
options: Trait A probably arose earlier, as rare traits are older ones.
Both traits arose together, as variations always arise in pairs.
Trait B probably arose earlier, as it has spread more widely.
Neither trait varies, as asexual species show no variation.
explanation: Correct option: (C). In asexual reproduction a variation is passed on to all descendants of the individual in which it arose, so a trait present in a larger share of the population has usually had more generations to spread and probably arose earlier. Rarity does not mean age, variations do not arise in pairs, and asexual species do show some variation.

stem: A man with blood group A marries a woman with blood group O, and their daughter has blood group O. What can be concluded about dominance?

Blood group A must be the dominant trait.
The data cannot settle which trait is dominant.

stem: Based on the case, what is the most likely genetic make-up of Asha's tall parent plant with violet flowers?

Hybrid tall (Tt) and pure violet (WW)
Hybrid tall (Tt) and hybrid violet (Ww)

stem: A pea plant is short although it grows in good conditions. Which explanation matches the chapter's account of how genes control height?

Its cells steadily lose DNA from their nuclei as the plant grows old.

stem: Why is the sex of a child in human beings decided by what the child inherits from the father?
options: Only the mother passes a Y chromosome on to her sons.
The father gives more DNA to the child than the mother.
Children get their sex chromosomes from the father only.
Only the father forms germ cells carrying either X or Y.
explanation: Correct option: (D). A woman is XX, so every egg carries an X. A man is XY, so half his sperms carry X and half carry Y; a child getting X from the father is a girl and one getting Y is a boy. Mothers never carry Y, both parents contribute practically equal DNA, and every child gets an X from the mother.

stem: A couple already has three daughters. What is the chance that their fourth child will be a boy?
options: More than one-half, as a son is now due.
One-half, as each birth is independent.
Zero, as this father gives only X to children.
Less than one-half, as daughters keep repeating.
explanation: Correct option: (B). At each fertilisation, the sperm is equally likely to carry X or Y, whatever happened in earlier births, so the chance of a boy is always one-half.
